subject: Function-fanout integration patterns & pilot plan
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Integration follow-up — function fanout, reranker options, and pilot

Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Use case: customer support assistant that executes actions (ticket creation, account lookup) + returns structured answer and a confidence-ranked suggestion list (reranker).
- Constraints: VPC/private endpoints preferred, embeddings stored ephemeral-only, tight latency requirement on core paths (<= 600ms P50).

Integration patterns we recommend to evaluate during a 2-week pilot (priority order):
1) Sequential function-calling (start here): model returns structured tool call; Redwood routes to single tool implementation synchronously. Simpler to debug and works for strong chain-of-thought flows.
2) Controlled parallel fanout: for non-blocking enrichments (external enrichment APIs, fraud checks) invoke in parallel, aggregate with a lightweight reranker to pick top result for the response. Good for hitting external SaaS during response generation.
3) Hybrid reranker pipeline: generate candidate outputs + embeddings -> dense/sparse reranker -> final structured outcome. Best for high-precision knowledge lookups.

Auth & SDK setup notes:
- We can support API key auth for initial pilot; for production we recommend OIDC service-to-service (with short-lived mTLS tokens) inside the VPC private deployment.
- Redwood JS/Go SDK has a 5-minute quickstart for function definitions and typed structured-output schemas.

Routing and error handling guidance:
- Route by latency SLO: pin primary region in pilot; fall back to cheaper model variant if primary unavailable.
- Error handling pattern: idempotent tool definitions + retry with exponential backoff for transient 5xx; circuit-breaker for persistent downstream failures; fallback to a best-effort model response when critical tool fails.

Attachments: redwood-integ-patterns-v1.pdf (patterns + cost tradeoffs), sample-prompt-set.csv (initial eval prompts).

Ask: Can you confirm the priorities (latency v accuracy v VPC) and availability for a technical deep-dive next Tue or Wed? If we get the green light we’ll spin up a 2-week pilot plan, share the prompt set, and have Marcus + Olga join the deep dive.

Thanks —
Jonas

Quick technical draft below — happy to walk through on the deep dive. Attachment: tool-definitions.yaml, routing-policy.md

High-level recommendation (pilot):
- Start with sequential function-calling for the critical user path (lowest risk, easy traceability).
- Offload non-critical enrichers to controlled parallel fanout with results aggregated asynchronously and surfaced via a reranker.

Tool definition (thin schema):
- id: string (stable identifier)
- name: string
- type: external_api | microservice | db_lookup
- inputs: json-schema (typed keys)
- outputs: json-schema (typed keys + confidence)
- timeout_ms: integer (default 1000)
- retry_policy: {strategy: "exponential_backoff", attempts: 3, backoff_ms: 200}
- idempotency_key: optional string (recommended for write operations)

Parallelism and orchestration:
- Use controlled concurrency (max_concurrency configurable per tenant). Start with max_concurrency=4 for the pilot.
- Use async queue for long-running enrichers, with webhook callback or polling.

Error handling & fallbacks:
- Transient 5xx: retry per retry_policy, emit trace and metric.
- Persistent failure: mark tool instance as degraded, circuit-breaker trips after configurable threshold, and use fallback (local cache or model-only response).
- For partial results from parallel fanout: use reranker scoring (embedding similarity + heuristic checks) to pick top candidate; if confidence < threshold, respond with model-only answer and log for human review.

Observability & compliance:
- Emit structured traces for each tool invocation (correlation_id, request_id, tool_id).
- Retention: configurable per account; for pilot recommend 90 days to satisfy SOC2 evidence requests.

Cost guidance (very rough):
- Sequential baseline: RPC overhead minimal; estimated delta = +15–25% token cost vs model-only for 10k sessions (depends on average tokens per tool call).
- Parallel fanout: extra API calls + embeddings for reranker; estimate +60–120% token/compute cost vs baseline for same traffic if all enrichers run in parallel. Recommend feature-flagged parallelism so we can gate usage during pilot.

I’ll prepare a one-page tech appendix and a sample tool-definitions.yaml for the deep dive.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
